summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with abdominal pain and fevers due to recurrent cholangitis in the setting of stage IV cholangiocarcinoma and biliary stents. Imaging showed biliary duct dilation suggesting obstruction. He underwent ERCP which cleared a blocked stent, relieving the obstruction. He was treated for bacteremia with broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed based on culture results, and for C. difficile infection with oral vancomycin. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic therapy. His condition improved with normalization of liver function tests and negative blood cultures. He was discharged home with a two-week course of IV cefepime and tigecycline, oral vancomycin, and instructions for drain care and follow-up.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of intrahepatic bile ducts
Other and unspecified Escherichia coli [E. coli]
